section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section provides the header for the maamar, including the Torah portion, month, and year.
section.t: With the help of Heaven.
Shabbos Parshas Chayei Sarah,
Erev Rosh Chodesh Kislev,
the year 5730.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section introduces the verse and the Rebbe's question about the repetition of "the years of Sarah's life," linking it to the Zohar's explanation of the verse "Viyitaron Eretz" and the concept of drawing down supernal lights into Malchus.
section.t: "And the life of Sarah was one hundred years and twenty years and seven years, the years of Sarah's life."
And the Rebbe
(the Rebbe Rashab)
of blessed memory, whose birthday is on the 20th of MarCheshvan, in his maamar beginning with the word "Zeh,"
notes: it already says "And the life of Sarah was,"
so why is it repeated again, "the years of Sarah's life"?
And he continues in the maamar,
that in the Zohar
on the verse "And the life of Sarah was," it first explains the verse
"The advantage of the land in everything is a king for a cultivated field."
And afterwards
it says that the matter of "And the life of Sarah was" is that Sarah merited supernal life.
And the maamar explains the connection of "The advantage of the land in everything is a king for a cultivated field" to "And the life of Sarah was,"
that "land" and "field" are aspects of Malchus,
and the matter of "the advantage of the land in everything is a king for a cultivated field" is the drawing down of lights that are above Malchus,
the aspect of "everything" and the aspect of "king,"
into Malchus.
And this is the connection of "The advantage of the land in everything is a king for a cultivated field" to "And the life of Sarah was,"
because Sarah is the aspect of Malchus
(analogous to "land" and "field"),
and that Sarah merited supernal life means that the lights that are above Malchus were drawn into her.
And it explains at length the four matters in the verse "The advantage of the land," etc.,
the two aspects in Malchus,
"land" and "field,"
and the two aspects in the lights that are above Malchus that are drawn into Malchus,
the aspect of "everything" and the aspect of "king."
And it explains,
that "twenty years and seven years" is in the manner of the aspect of "everything,"
and "one hundred years" is in the manner of the aspect of "king."
And after this it explains
(at the conclusion of the maamar),
that "And the life of Sarah was" is the drawing down of supernal life
(one hundred years and twenty years and seven years)
into Malchus,
and "the years of Sarah's life" is
that the supernal life was drawn down into Biyah (the worlds of Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah).
And it must be understood,

that in order to explain the addition of "the years of Sarah's life" over "And the life of Sarah was," it seemingly only matters that "And the life of Sarah was" is the drawing down of supernal life into Malchus,
for based on this it can be explained that the addition of "the years of Sarah's life" is the drawing down into Biyah,
and from the fact that this explanation comes
(in the maamar)
after the explanation of the verse "The advantage of the land," etc., and its connection to "And the life of Sarah was,"
it implies
that through this, additional explanation is added in the matter of "the years of Sarah's life"
(the drawing down into Biyah).

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the distinction between "land" and "field" as external and internal aspects of Malchus, and how the advantage of the land is the drawing down of the aspect of "everything" (Yesod) and the revelation of Ein Sof through the service of mitzvos in the field (Gan Eden).
section.t: B)
And this will be understood based on what is explained in the maamar
about the difference between "land" and "field,"
that "land" is the entirety of the world,
and "field"
(the choicest part of the land)
is the Garden of Eden.
And this distinction between the entirety of the world and the Garden of Eden
(that the entirety of the world is called "land" and the Garden of Eden is called "field")
is in their source.
For the creation of the world is from the aspect of the externality of Malchus, which is called "land,"
and the Garden of Eden is from the aspect of the internality of Malchus, which is called "field."
And the maamar continues,
that just as the advantage of the field in its simple sense is that it is a place suitable for sowing,
so too regarding the Garden of Eden,
it is a place prepared for the drawing down of the revelation of the Ein Sof
(growth)
through the sowing of the mitzvos.
[And as explained elsewhere
on the verse
"And Hashem Elokim took the man and placed him in the Garden of Eden to work it and to guard it," and our sages said
"to work it" refers to the 248 positive commandments, and "to guard it" refers to the 365 negative commandments,
the reason for this, that He placed him in the Garden of Eden
(specifically)
to work it and to guard it,
is
because the Garden of Eden is a place prepared for the revelation that is drawn down through the fulfillment of the mitzvos.
And that the revelation is drawn down through the fulfillment of the mitzvos in the entirety of the world
(after man was banished from the Garden of Eden)
is as it is written
"And Hashem Elokim sent him out of the Garden of Eden to work the ground," etc.,
that the matter of "to work the ground" is to make the place of the world prepared for revelation].
And this is "The advantage of the land in everything is a king for a cultivated field,"
that the advantage of the land
[the entirety of the world,
whose creation is from the externality of Malchus]
is "in everything,"
that the aspect of "everything" is drawn into it,
which is the Sefirah of Yesod, which is called "everything."
And "a king for a cultivated field" is the drawing down of the revelation of the Ein Sof
(which is above the aspect of "everything")
through the fulfillment of the mitzvos.
As it is stated in the Zohar there,
"Who is a king? That is the supernal King who unites with the field when it is cultivated,"
that through the service in the Garden of Eden
("cultivated field")
which is the service of fulfilling the mitzvos
("to work it" refers to the 248 positive commandments, and "to guard it" refers to the 365 negative commandments),
the revelation of the Ein Sof is drawn down
(the supernal King),
which is above the revelation of the aspect of "everything."
